item.title: K-5 Grading System Changes for 2026-2027
item.description:
Starting in the 2026-2027 school year, Talawanda is changing its elementary grading systems:

  • Grades 3-5: Moving to traditional letter grades (A-F) to align with middle/high school expectations (A=90-100%, B=80-89%, C=70-79%, D=60-69%, F=0-59%)
  • Grades K-2: Continuing with the numerical system (1-4) where 4=Consistently/Independently Meeting Standard, 3=Meeting Standard, 2=Approaching Standard, 1=Not Yet Meeting Standard

This change prepares upper elementary students for future academic expectations while maintaining developmentally appropriate assessment for younger learners.

item.title: Understanding Bullying and Peer Conflict
item.description:
Bullying is unwanted, aggressive behavior involving a real or perceived power imbalance that is repeated over time. For behavior to be considered bullying, it must include both an imbalance of power (using physical strength, access to embarrassing information, or popularity to control or harm others) and repetition (happening more than once or having potential to happen again). Bullying actions include making threats, spreading rumors, physical or verbal attacks, and purposeful exclusion. Peer conflict is different—it occurs when two kids with no perceived power imbalance fight, argue, or disagree, and is not considered bullying. Adults can help children develop age-appropriate conflict resolution skills.

item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game School-Wide Implementation
item.description:
Kramer Elementary School is implementing the PAX Good Behavior Game (PAX GBG) school-wide, an evidence-based strategy to help students build self-regulation, focus, and teamwork. Key concepts include PAX Behaviors (positive actions), SPLEEMS (minor disruptions to reduce), PAX Quiet (attention signal using harmonica), Tootles (notes recognizing kind acts), and PAX Prizes (activity breaks earned by keeping SPLEEMS low). Families can support by asking children about their PAX experiences and using PAX concepts at home during daily routines.

item.title: Understanding Bullying vs. Peer Conflict
item.description:
Bullying is unwanted, aggressive behavior involving a power imbalance and repetition (or potential for repetition). It includes making threats, spreading rumors, physical or verbal attacks, and intentional exclusion. Peer conflict is different—when two kids with no power imbalance fight, argue, or disagree, it's not bullying. Conflict resolution or peer mediation can help address peer conflicts appropriately.

item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game School-Wide Implementation
item.description:
Kramer Elementary School is implementing the PAX Good Behavior Game (PAX GBG) school-wide, an evidence-based strategy to help students build self-regulation, focus, and teamwork. Key terms students will use include PAX Behaviors (positive actions), SPLEEMS (minor disruptions to reduce), PAX Quiet (attention signal using harmonica), Tootles (notes recognizing kind acts), and PAX Prizes (30-second activity breaks earned by reducing SPLEEMS). Families can support PAX at home by asking children about their PAX experiences and choices throughout the day.

item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game Classroom Strategies
item.description:
Students will be learning in a PAX classroom this year, using evidence-based strategies to practice self-regulation, cooperation, and focused learning. PAX strategies include PAX Vision (setting clear expectations), Wacky Prizes (fun rewards), Beat the Timer (task completion), PAX Stix (fair participation), Tootle Notes (recognizing others' good behavior), PAX OK/Not OK (non-verbal feedback), and the PAX Good Behavior Game (team-based self-regulation). Parents are encouraged to ask their children about these strategies to support learning at home.
